recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future charset-negotiation or generic MIME response changes should be handled through the later HTTP issue family rather than reopening FHIR-6121.
issue_request: FHIR-6121 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core-http. The request asked to clarify Content-Type, _format, Accept, and Accept-Charset; the final resolution required clarifying that _format only overrides Accept and not Content-Type.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 5961, imported as git commit 49a0a0f517e8e3a32f70c93f49df5c077d7ead38 (#6121 - clarify the use of _format header), which changed source/http.html to say _format overrides the accept header and added a note that it does not override content-type.
additional_context: source/http.html is in current build scope through source/hierarchy.xml. Later HTTP-page decisions refined neighboring MIME and encoding guidance: FHIR-8978 added the undefined response MIME case when neither Accept nor _format is supplied, FHIR-9029 reorganized generic Accept/_format behavior while preserving the Content-Type limitation, and FHIR-16343 removed stale Accept-Charset/default-charset prose in favor of current UTF-8 guidance.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current source/http.html says _format specifies alternative response formats, overrides the accept header value, and does not override the Content-Type header for the body type of a POST request; its UTF-8 wording also makes reintroducing Accept-Charset prose inappropriate for this old issue.
